editorial:
Imagine if a simple medical mistake led to a baby being born with the instincts of a caveman. That is exactly what happens here. You follow Dr. James Mydell, a scientist who is juggling two very different projects. He is trying to get DNA from a prehistoric man found in ice, while also helping his friends, the Cordells, start a family. In a clumsy moment, he mixes up the samples, and Elaine Cordell ends up pregnant with a child from the Bronze Age. It sounds like a wild B-movie plot, and that is exactly the vibe it goes for. It is a mix of science fiction and family drama that keeps you wondering how a modern household handles a kid who is built for the wild.

The acting is surprisingly solid for a TV movie, and the way the child grows and changes is the best part. While the special effects are a bit dated, the tension keeps the story moving fast. If you enjoy weird science plots with a bit of heart, you will love this. Since it is an older flick, you might want to look for a high-quality digital version. It is best enjoyed streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the clearest picture, or you could grab the 4K Blu-ray to keep in your physical collection for a rainy day.
endingExplained: The story wraps up as the boy's prehistoric instincts become too strong for a normal city life. He grows rapidly and shows strength and aggression that scare the parents. In the end, the family realizes he cannot fit into modern society. He eventually finds a way to connect with his wild roots, leaving the parents to deal with the guilt of the experiment. It ends with the bittersweet realization that some things should stay in the past.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school science gone wrong movies.
